Subject: Exec spotcheck: priorities, wins, gaps — week of 2027-05-20

Team — sending a short, prioritized snapshot ahead of Friday's QBR prep call. Keeping this crisp: wins, current gaps/risks, and three asks where I need support or decisions. See attached OKR snapshot and the QBR prep asks doc.

Wins:
- Serving runtime: End-to-end latency SLOs improved across p50/p95 for small-scale chat (p95 down 18% week-over-week after kernel tweak).
- Redwood Dedicated: Early beta for reserved bursts completed validation tests on N.Virginia hardware (throughput +13%).
- Console: New trace UI rolled out to 20% of accounts; initial CS feedback positive — fewer manual debug sessions.

Gaps / Risks:
- Private deployment onboarding: two customers stalled on network config (VPC peering edge case). Risk: potential delay to two private deals in SRE backlog.
- Capacity for peak demo days: our current Dedicated pools will be near-saturated for the Acme POC (deal D-4892). If we can't carve burst capacity, we risk delaying the demo by a week.
- QBR narrative: we still need updated cost-per-token numbers for quantized workloads (finance + infra metric alignment).

Asks (priority order):
1) Vivek — confirm by EOD whether we can commit one extra Reserved pod for Acme POC (details in HubSpot D-4892).
2) Jonas — please work with infra to unblock VPC peering checklist; if it needs an exception, escalate to infra leadership and loop me in.
3) Laura & Maya — review the QBR prep doc and flag any slide edits (permissions to the deck attached). I'm consolidating changes by Friday 10:00 PT.

Attachments: 20270520-OKR-snapshot.png, QBR-prep-asks.docx

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clean summary, Stephanie. Quick notes:

- Acme POC (D-4892): We can provision an extra Reserved pod for the demo window but only for a 72-hour pre-booked window. That will require a signed addendum (procurement). If Sales can push DocuSign today, infra can schedule the pod.

- Capacity headroom: infra telemetry shows Dedicated pools at ~78% utilization during peak. We have two mitigation options — short-term: burst pods (what I referenced above); medium-term: increase autoscale ceiling on pool A (requires budget sign-off).

- VPC peering issue: noted. Jonas — will assign an infra on-call to pair with the customer's network engineer today. If you hit a policy block, escalate to security and cc me.

On cost-per-token: finance is reconciling a minor discrepancy between the quantized runtime accounting and the billing meter. I asked them for a reconciliation spreadsheet; expect an update tomorrow morning.

Vivek
